workflow: A loader accepts a serialized executable object containing truncated or incompatible variable-length location metadata.
A lazy metadata reader decodes continuation fields without verifying that each read remains within the metadata buffer.
The reader advances past the buffer and interprets adjacent memory as additional location data.
Downstream processing uses the invalid decoded values, corrupting memory and eventually crashing instead of rejecting the malformed object.
summary: Unchecked variable-length metadata decoding causes adjacent-memory access and later corruption
decision_reason: The underlying failure workflow materially matches the existing cluster: malformed truncated metadata is decoded without bounds checks, causing reads beyond the metadata buffer and downstream memory-safety failure. The affected metadata and observed crash differ, but the causal mechanism is the same
